A Complex Market Environment

The past few months on Wall Street have been confusing, complex, and often contradictory. On the one hand, U.S bond yields have reached their highest level since 2002, oil prices have soared, the War in Iran has yet to conclude, and market breadth (participation) has been atrocious. Meanwhile, the major market indices have been extremely resilient. For instance, in the normally seasonally brutal September, the Nasdaq 100 Index ETF (QQQ) gained 3%. The tech-heavy index is now less than 1% away from all time-highs.

Instead of relying on gut feel and news headlines, investors should rely on historical data sets. From this perspective, bulls may be in for a pleasant fall surprise. Below are 5 reasons why.

1. Breadth Washout: Bluekurtic Market Insights (@Bluekurtic) notes that fewer than 42% of S&P 500 stocks are above their 200-day moving averages. "In prior cases, SPX was higher 5 days later 100% of the time."

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Bluekurtic Market Insights

2. AI Growth Remains Robust: Micron (MU) is one of the best barometers of the strength of the AI boom. Wednesday, Micron delivered a massive earnings report, including record profits. Micron is now generating a blistering $553 million in revenue per day! Read more about Micron's earnings here.

3. October Seasonality Is Not So Spooky: According to data from Ryan Detrick of Carson Investment Research, October is the strongest month of the midterm-year seasonality calendar. Better yet, November is the second strongest.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Carson Invesment Research

4. Treasury Yield Recency Bias: The biggest fear on Wall Street currently is that the 30-year Treasury yield is over 5% (which can mean lower valuations). However, as Charlie Bilello of Creative Planning points out, "That seems really high until you zoom out and learn that the yield was actually higher than this every single day in the 1980s and 92% of days in the 1990s." Despite perceived high yields, these two decades were fantastic times to be long U.S. equity markets.

5. Tech Valuations are Reasonable: Despite the hype around AI and tech stocks, their valuations remain reasonable. In fact, Alphabet (GOOGL), Meta Platforms (META), and Microsoft (MSFT) all have price-to-earnings ratios that are below 30x.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

Bottom Line

While market contradictions and macro headlines can spark investor anxiety, historical data and strong fundamentals suggest bulls have plenty to cheer about this fall.

Enterprises that keep their source code behind their own firewalls now have a way to run Bob, the agentic software development platform from IBM (NYSE:IBM), on infrastructure they control. IBM stock is at $231.05, up 5% in morning trading.

Sundry Photography / iStock Editorial via Getty Images

That gain stands well apart from the rest of software, which points to a repricing of IBM shares specifically. Meanwhile, the iShares Expanded Tech-Software Sector ETF (CBOE:IGV) is at $107.95, up 1.4%. The Invesco QQQ Trust (NASDAQ:QQQ), which tracks the NASDAQ 100, is at $743.84, up 0.6%.

Self-Hosted Bob Targets Regulated Enterprises

A new IBM release extends Bob to on-premises, private-cloud, sovereign-cloud and air-gapped environments that the customer controls. Under IBM's self-hosted option, enterprises can run supported models on their own infrastructure, including air-gapped systems, or connect Bob to approved external AI services in hybrid configurations.

The self-hosted option serves organizations that require control over data residency, security policies, governance and software development workflows, a profile that fits much of IBM's installed base. Neel Sundaresan, General Manager of AI and Automation at IBM, stated in the release: "The future of enterprise AI will depend on security, governance and sovereignty." By running Bob where a customer's code, application context and data already are located, IBM removes an concern that has kept regulated and sovereignty-constrained enterprises off public coding platforms.

title: Microsoft stock best quarter since 1998: Q3 2026 gains 37.5%
detail:
Microsoft stock best quarter since 1998: Q3 2026 gains 37.5%
Quartz · Bloomberg / Getty Images
Cris Tolomia
Thu, October 1, 2026 at 6:43 AM CDT 2 min read

^NDX
Trade MSFT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Microsoft stock surged 37.5% across the third quarter, a performance unmatched since 1998 that lifted the company's market capitalization by $1 trillion, according to Bloomberg. The stock was the fifth-best performer in the Nasdaq 100 Index over that period; the index itself gained just 0.4% over the same three months.

Much of the gain followed Microsoft's earnings report in late July, which showed cloud growth at its fastest pace in four years, driven by demand for AI products. That single-day move of 16% was the stock's strongest showing in nearly two decades, dating back to October 2008, and brought $450 billion in new market value.

The quarterly rally marked a sharp reversal from June, when the stock logged its weakest monthly showing in roughly 25 years amid widespread skepticism about the company's AI outlays and what a world dominated by AI might mean for software vendors.

"After a period where it struggled with the message, Microsoft has been crisper and cleaner on how it will monetize its capital outlay and benefit its customers," said Chad Morganlander, senior portfolio manager at Washington Crossing Advisors, according to Bloomberg. "It is showing a clear path to profitability with AI. As a company that is spending but not going into the red on account, it looks like the adult in the room."

Among the other large AI spenders — Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta — Microsoft is the only one that has not seen free cash flow turn negative on an annual basis, according to Bloomberg.

Wall Street sentiment has shifted. Among the 72 Bloomberg-tracked analysts covering Microsoft, buy ratings account for all but three, and not a single analyst recommends selling the stock. Last week, Stifel analyst Brad Reback upgraded the stock to buy, writing that the company had "clearly turned the corner," according to the outlet.

"Investors realized they misunderstood the company's potential, so a lot of the rally is just the reversal of that mistake," said JoAnne Feeney, portfolio manager at Advisors Capital Management, according to the outlet.

Even after the quarter's outsized move, Microsoft has returned only 6.1% on a year-to-date basis, a figure that falls well short of the Nasdaq 100's 20% advance.

US stock futures were mixed on Thursday ahead of the first trading session of the fourth quarter, with investors assessing higher Treasury yields, Micron's (NASDAQ:MU) latest outlook and upcoming economic data.

At 03:34 ET (07:34 GMT), Dow futures were down 219 points, or 0.4%, while S&P 500 futures gained 4 points, or 0.1%. Nasdaq 100 futures rose 161 points, or 0.5%.

The major US indices also recorded mixed performances in the previous session, with the S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average declining while the Nasdaq Composite advanced.

US Treasury yields moved higher despite August personal consumption expenditures inflation coming in below expectations. Attention is now turning to September employment data for further information on the US Federal Reserve's interest-rate outlook.

During September, the S&P 500 declined 0.45% and the Dow fell 4.29%, while the Nasdaq gained 1.86%. The Nasdaq and S&P 500 recorded their second consecutive quarterly gains, while the Dow declined during the July-to-September period.

Micron Shares Rise Following Revenue Forecast

Micron shares moved higher in extended trading after the semiconductor manufacturer issued a quarterly revenue forecast above market expectations.

The company said customer commitments under long-term supply agreements had increased to $32 billion from $22 billion reported in June.

Demand for memory chips has increased alongside investment in data centres used for artificial intelligence applications. Micron supplies memory products to customers including Nvidia.

Micron shares have more than tripled since the beginning of the year, according to the supplied data.

Nike Results Due After Market Close

Nike (NYSE:NKE) shares were slightly lower in after-hours trading ahead of the company's latest financial results.

The results will provide an update on the strategy being implemented under chief executive Elliott Hill, including a greater focus on sports such as football and running, relationships with wholesale partners and new product launches.

Nike has faced weaker sales and increased competition. Its shares have fallen more than 44% since the beginning of the year, according to the supplied data.

S&P Dow Jones removed Nike from the S&P 100 during September as part of its quarterly rebalancing, ending the company's 18-year inclusion in the index.

US Manufacturing Data Awaited

Investors are also awaiting the Institute for Supply Management's September manufacturing purchasing managers' index.

The index is expected to rise to 54.8 from 54.6 in August. A reading above 50 indicates an expansion in manufacturing activity.
